body:
## Summary
The stream-prep rules (counts, lines per kind, payoff, connector kinds) are written four times: prompt prose, JSON schema, the mechanical checks and the CLI guide. They have already drifted: the gate that holds approval is looser than what the planner is told and constrained to. Make one `prep::rules` table and render the prompt text, the reply schema, the checks and a doc-asserting test from it.

## Description
Registry: review-iteration-loops, technique `critique-carries-its-fix` (a gate whose rules differ from the brief it judges cannot be gated on; law unmeasured-is-not-pass). The system prompt (planner.rs:24) claims a mechanical checker enforces the rules, yet a callback of 4+ lines (schema cap 3, planner.rs:226) or a premise/callback without a payoff (schema-required, planner.rs:198) passes `shape` (checks.rs:265-268) and can be approved (store.rs:246). The connector-kind list is typed twice (planner.rs:233 vs checks.rs:32). `rules.rs` holds `BitRule { kind, count: (min, Option<max>), lines: (min, max), payoff_required }`, the cold-open beat range, MAX_LINE_CHARS, CONNECTOR_KINDS derived from the enum, and renderers `prompt_lines()`, `schema_for(kind)`, `doc_rows()`. checks.rs loops over the table; check ids stay as they are (no contract change, no overlap with the types-crate check-id card). Gate: policy-tighten - the approval gate becomes exactly as strict as what the planner was already told.

## Flow
- rules.rs: the table and its renderers
- planner.rs: prompt and schema render from rules (literals deleted)
- checks.rs: counts/shape iterate the rule rows; callback 1-3 lines and a payoff on every bit enforced
- tests.rs: drift tests (schema == table, prompt contains table text, doc rows == table) plus the two tightened cases
- docs/guide/cli.md: rows regenerated

## Expected impact
One edit point for every prep rule; the planner's promise and the owner's approval gate become the same rule set; the bug class recorded at planner.rs:189 (schema and intent diverging) becomes a failing test.

## Evaluation
Claim: the approval gate enforces exactly what the planner is told, from one table.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (4-line callback and payoff-less premise pass the gate; enum and counts are literals; the doc is unchecked)
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: planner.rs:167 `- callbacks: {}-{} running gags from the bible, re-dressed for tonight, needing no earlier stream (1-3 lines each, with a payoff)`; planner.rs:226 `"callbacks": bits(CALLBACKS.0, Some(CALLBACKS.1), 1, 3)`; planner.rs:198 `"required": ["segment", "lines", "payoff"]`; planner.rs:233 `"enum": ["into_room", "into_bit", "back_to_chat", "into_poll", "into_handover"]`; checks.rs:265 `BitKind::Callback if n == 0 => shape.push(...)`; checks.rs:268 `if b.kind == BitKind::Story && b.payoff.as_deref().is_none_or(...)`; characters/malakor/prep.sample.json: callbacks have 1-2 lines and all 20 bits carry a payoff, so the tightened gate keeps the sample green.

critic.reason: Real gate/brief drift on the approval path, closed from one table with tests that fail on the next drift.

title: `prep revise`: answer failed checks with an edit plan, not a full regenerate
acceptance: staged prep failing only `urls` on conn-01; fake planner returns [{op: rewrite, target: conn-01, line, why}] -> a new staged prep id with all 9 checks passing; every line except conn-01 byte-identical to the base; exit 0
fake planner also returns a rewrite of prem-04 (named by no finding and no note) -> that op lands in revision.json refused_ops with reason 'target not named'; prem-04 unchanged in the new prep
base fails `counts` with '2 into_poll connectors (at least 3)' -> the finding is an insert slot of kind into_poll; an insert op adds conn-16 [into_poll]; counts passes
base with 11 failing lines -> the revision prompt names all 11 locators (no 'and N more' truncation as at checks.rs:134)
`prep revise <id> --note 'cb-02: too flat'` on an all-pass staged prep -> cb-02 is a legal target; result staged; the base prep.json bytes are unchanged and it stays staged
revise of an approved or retired prep -> exit 1, conflict; a planner reply that echoes the fence token -> nothing staged, exit 1
`prep show <new>` -> prints 'revised from <base>: N ops' with each op's target and why; <data>/prep/<new>/revision.json holds the base id, findings, ops and refused_ops

docs/guide/cli.md:368 - 'the fix is a new `prep generate`': the only repair path is a whole new planner call

crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/prep/checks.rs:134 - failure detail is prose truncated to 8 problems ('and N more'): neither the owner nor a next stage sees every failing line
crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/prep/checks.rs:102 - every line already has a stable locator (`prem-03 line 1`, `conn-01`, `cold_open.beats[2]`) usable as an edit target
crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/prep/cli.rs:28 - PrepCommand is generate/list/show/approve/retire only; nothing acts on what `show` reports
crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/e2e/prep.rs:156 - one tainted connector (conn-01) fails the whole prep
crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/prep/planner.rs:141 - UntrustedFence already wraps model-composed text; the revision prompt reuses it for the base material
rollback: Additive: a new subcommand, revise.rs and a findings() fn beside run(). Reverting the series removes `prep revise`; revised preps already staged stay ordinary staged preps (revision.json is an unread sidecar).

runner_up: `prep rehearse <id>`: a judged scripted sandbox minute pinned to a STAGED prep, so the owner approves with per-bit landed/flat evidence instead of blind (needs sandbox.rs, overlapping the sim-runner-judging card)
body:
## Summary
When a staged prep fails one check on one line, the owner's only path is `prep generate` again: a fresh planner call that rewrites all ~73 lines, discards everything that passed and that they already read, and may fail a different check. `prep revise <id> [--note '<locator>: text']...` answers the failing lines (and the owner's notes) with a closed edit plan - rewrite / cut / insert on named locators - applies it, stages the result as a new prep and re-runs every check.

## Description
Registry: review-iteration-loops, techniques `edit-plan-over-regeneration` (the revision deliverable is a list of operations; lines no operation names stay byte-identical) and `critique-carries-its-fix` (each finding names its location and the whole class is swept, not truncated). checks.rs gains `findings(p, ctx) -> Vec<Finding { check, at, why, slot }>`, the same predicates run() uses, untruncated, with count shortfalls expressed as insert slots; run() keeps building its prose (check ids and wire unchanged: no contract edit). revise.rs builds the prompt (base material fenced with UntrustedFence, findings and owner notes as the only legal targets), a schema with a closed op enum, and `apply(base, plan) -> (StreamPrep, refused_ops)` that refuses any op whose target is not a finding or a note. The new prep is staged through the existing locked store; revision.json beside it keeps base id, findings, ops and refusals. The approval gate is untouched: the revised prep must pass every check like any other. Both of this context's cards edit checks.rs: if both are approved, land A first and B rebases (disjoint functions).

## Flow
- `prep revise <id>` -> load the staged base -> findings + notes -> one planner call (edit plan) -> apply -> full checks -> stage a new id + revision.json -> print the summary; exit 0 / 6 as generate does
- `prep show` prints lineage and ops
- the base prep is never mutated

## Expected impact
A one-line failure costs one targeted call and a re-read of the changed lines, not a whole new prep and a full re-read. The owner's notes become actionable (today `show` reports and nothing acts). Approval effort scales with the notes, not the material.

## Evaluation
Claim: a failed or noted staged prep is repaired in one command, untouched lines byte-identical.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no revise command; detail truncated at 8)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first (fake planner engine as in prep/tests.rs)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: store.rs:237-239 `"prep {id} failed {}: a failed check holds and no override applies; generate a new prep"`; checks.rs:134-137 `problems.into_iter().take(8)` ... `detail.push_str(&format!("; and {} more", n - 8))`; cli.rs:28-69 `enum PrepCommand { Generate, List, Show, Approve, Retire }`; e2e/prep.rs:35 taints only connectors[0] and :155-156 assert the urls check fails naming conn-01 while the rest is clean; the sample prep's line_length detail reads '73 lines'.

critic.reason: New, scoped owner capability with strong guard cases and no change to the approval gate.
